answer.evidence: radon/complexity.py:10-12 defines the sort keys: SCORE = -GET_COMPLEXITY(block) (descending complexity), LINES = block.lineno, ALPHA = block.name. radon/complexity.py:59-75 sorted_results(blocks, order=SCORE) is a thin wrapper over sorted(blocks, key=order). Review points: ALPHA is case-sensitive, so uppercase names sort before lowercase. SCORE and LINES give no tie-breaker beyond Python's stable sort. The default is SCORE. radon/cli/__init__.py:160 resolves the user's order string with getattr(cc_mod, order.upper(), SCORE), so an invalid value silently falls back to SCORE. radon/visitors.py is where the blocks get their lineno, name and complexity attributes, so the 'measured block' objects those keys read from are reviewed there (Function/Class lineno, name, and the complexity property). Note that a Class's complexity may differ from a Function's, which affects SCORE ordering. radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py take no part in block ordering and need only a brief check. Tests in radon/tests/test_cli.py and test_cli_harvest.py only exercise SCORE, so LINES and ALPHA are untested through the CLI path.
